binding.limit: byte agreement, argv equality and a re-parsed XML; not proof that a human ran the command

ci.limit: structure only: this gate cannot show that GitHub ran the job, only that nothing can skip it

oneTokenizerPerFile.note: one lexer, three projections; measured on the sources and on a deterministic corpus

proofLayers.ci: the step that runs this gate sits in a job a push or pull request reaches, and nothing can skip it
proofLayers.executed: the surefire XML of an offline run: the assembly cases really invoked the production bean method, and the binder certificate reports the name Spring's own loaders resolved
proofLayers.notProven: that a human rather than a text editor produced the recorded run; that GitHub executed the CI job; a config layer outside the recorded surface; a condition javac cannot fold
proofLayers.staticStructure: the guard call is a statement an assembly reaches, and the guard clauses are live code rather than prose; auxiliary to the executed proof and blind to a condition javac cannot fold
proofLayers.textCensus: agreement of the contract anchors, every config declaration this census can attribute and the Java constant, all read after JLS 3.3 translation

staticCallSite.basis: direct statement of the assembled bean identitySecurity, every enclosing condition is open or compile-time satisfiable and no unconditional transfer precedes it

agreement.textCensusLimit: attributed by text: block and flow mappings, multi-line flow, comments, quoting and case variants. Not attributed by text: anchors, merge keys, tags, block scalars and placeholders - those files are judged by the binder certificate below, which is why their bytes have to be in the recorded run.
